candidates.decision_relevance: Would show whether reported breadth weakness or recovery persisted, rather than relying on asynchronous endpoint snapshots with changing proxy membership.
candidates.evidence_reference: W41 review: quantitative breadth sequences are not supplied; daily reviews repeatedly note point-in-time proxy breadth, differing memberships, and missing aligned history.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped breadth counts and returns on a consistently defined universe
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied breadth observations are sparse or asynchronous, often use different membership, and do not establish the timing or persistence of participation changes.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would permit checking whether relative leadership and price deterioration preceded, coincided with, or followed the reported drawdowns and rebounds.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews note unavailable or short actual API horizons and limited event sequencing; W39–W41 reviews identify absent aligned quantitative paths.
candidates.metric_name: Synchronized hourly BTC, ETH, and ETH/BTC price-return series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Window summaries and partial hourly observations do not provide a continuous, common-timestamp history sufficient to inspect lead-lag and persistence.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would clarify whether spot participation and liquidity conditions weakened persistently or only in brief snapshots, and how they aligned with price moves.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews describe venue-specific spot depth and taker-flow readings as brief snapshots; weekly reviews repeatedly identify missing spot-participation and liquidity sequences.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped spot depth and aggressive-flow observations
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied microstructure evidence is sparse and short-window, preventing assessment of persistence or event order; fragile liquidation aggregates are not a substitute.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would allow auditing forecast range containment, timing, and errors against the information available when each candidate was issued, without treating immature or retrospective observations as validation.
candidates.evidence_reference: Multiple weekly and daily reviews report omitted candidate definitions, issue times, evidence cutoffs, bounds, and matured candidate-linked outcomes.
candidates.metric_name: Frozen forecast-candidate records with point-in-time evidence snapshots and matured realized outcomes
candidates.missing_history_problem: Candidate counts or aggregate calibration summaries are supplied without the specifications and timestamped outcomes needed to reconstruct ex-ante evaluations.
